title: Mayor
statement: Oakland does not need another Ivy Hill announcement; it needs a disciplined council review of the legislation already filed. I am taking up INIT-014, the $2.5M Ivy Hill Community Support Initiative, as a Proposed measure with a C116 vote scheduled—not as a funded or completed program. Ivy Hill's sentiment has improved from -0.14 to -0.06, and retail vitality from 5.17 to 5.54, but the neighborhood still trails the city's 0.107 sentiment reading. Those facts argue for careful delivery, not an emergency script. I welcome Council President Vega's scrutiny and the Council's fiscal and process questions. My work this week is to make the scope, safeguards and implementation record clear before any vote is claimed.

payload.text: Clerk-backed status, stated without overclaiming: the current tracker records INIT-014 legislation as filed at C115 and now lists the $2.5M initiative as vote-scheduled for C116. Its stage remains Proposed. That corrects my earlier 'unverified filing' formulation; it does not establish a passed vote, funding, delivery or completion, and no roll call is supplied here. For the C114–C116 complaint display, the record shows 11 complaints and 14 constructive-participation entries. The visible subject mapping is: West Oakland—INIT-001 disbursement and household documentation; Fruitvale—stalled INIT-007; Uptown/Grand Lake—police clearance and accountability; Ivy Hill—empty storefronts and the conditions behind INIT-014; Lake Merritt—health-care and civic-life items. My office owns answers on INIT-001, INIT-007 and INIT-014; the clearance item requires the responsible public-safety case record. The packet lacks full docket IDs, assigned owners, remedies and next dates, so none of these entries should be represented as resolved.
